Hi Rachel,

We're finalizing our SIG response and the CAIQ reviewers asked for a concise narrative and network diagrams that show how Redwood isolates customer workloads in both Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically they want:

- A short (1-2 page) narrative describing control-plane vs data-plane separation and where customer keys and audit logs live.
- A network diagram for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) showing tenant isolation, ingress/egress controls, and autoscaling/bursting boundaries.
- A network diagram for Private (VPC/on-prem) that highlights the private control plane option, transit routing, and KMS boundaries.
- List of controls/guardrails that ensure no cross-tenant KV cache leakage during model inference windows.

We originally asked for this in the RFI but SIG insisted on annotated artifacts. Can you confirm if you can deliver these by EOD Thursday (10/22)? If not, a short interim statement that we can include would also help.

Rachel / Kim — adding the technical bits below for the KV cache and runtime isolation section. I'll include these verbatim in the narrative unless you want edits.

--- quoted for inclusion ---
Control-plane vs data-plane separation (summary):
- Control plane: managed services owned by Redwood (or customer-hosted control plane in Private mode). Runs in a logically separated management VPC. Access is restricted via IAM and mutual-TLS to inference nodes. Audit logs and orchestration metadata are retained in the control plane; customer model artifacts can be configured to live in customer-managed buckets for Private deployments.
- Data plane (inference runtime): resides in tenant-specific pools for Dedicated, and in customer VPCs for Private. For Dedicated we implement tenant affinity scheduling so an inference job is placed only on nodes assigned to the tenant's reserved pool. For Private, the runtime may be deployed in the customer's VPC or on-premises and is reachable only over configured peering/VPN.

Runtime isolation and KV cache handling:
- KV cache is instantiated in-process for each model session; cache memory is tagged per-session and cleared on session termination. We enforce strict memory isolation and periodic guardrails that zero sensitive buffers after eviction.
- For Dedicated: worker nodes are hypervisor-isolated per-tenant pool; we run an LSM (Linux Security Module) profile and container runtime policies to prevent cross-tenant IPC. A short retention-only telemetry buffer is written to a tenant-isolated metrics service; no raw token streams are persisted.
- For Private (VPC/on-prem): customers control network egress and KMS. Redwood's private control plane (optional) only sends signed control messages; any customer-requested artifacts (models, keys) can remain under customer KMS.

Mitigations for noisy neighbour and burst scenarios:
- Autoscaling occurs within tenant pools; burst capacity uses pre-provisioned ephemeral instances tagged to the tenant and scrubbed on decommission.
- Fallback routing to multi-tenant shared capacity is only permitted with explicit contract allowances and has additional logical isolation layers and rate limits.

--- end quote ---

Attachments I'll produce: control-plane-narrative_v1.pdf, isolation-diagram_v2.png.

If reviewers push for packet-level evidence, we can provide sanitized flow logs and a PCAP-lite (metadata-only) extract but that is last resort.
